newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch seen keeping cap on gas, oil production cost.
newsitem.headline: Dutch seen keeping cap on gas, oil production cost.

text.p: The Dutch are expected to keep a tight rein on gas and oil production costs in the next five years despite the steady maturing of its production fields, according to a report by consultants Wood Mackenzie.
"A lot of fields are quite mature now. (Operators in the Netherlands) have kept lead times short. For a mature area, they're doing pretty well," said a Wood Mackenzie consultant.
Operating costs for offshore production are expected to average 7.1 guilders ($4.3) per barrel of oil equivalent (boe) in 1997, a fall of 25 percent in real terms from 1993.
In the period 1997-2002, average operating costs will only increase slightly to 7.5 guilders per boe.

"The impact of higher cost production from mature fields with declining production levels is offset, to a large extent, by low cost production from recent and upcoming new field developments," Wood Mackenzie says in a summary of its report.
Offshore, Amoco is the lowest cost operator.
Onshore, operating costs are expected to average 2.2 guilders ($1.3) per boe, a fall of 29 percent in real terms from their late 1988-1990 peak.
Onshore production is dominated by NAM's giant low-cost Groningen gas field which masks the impact of higher cost fields. NAM is jointly owned by Exxon and Royal Dutch/Shell.
By the year 2002, Wood Mackenzie expects onshore operating costs to rise by 14 percent in real terms to 2.5 guilders per boe, while output is set to decline by six percent.
